additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly calls the trembling of Adam's limbs (when God told him he would eat grass) a bechina of the fever illness. 'נִזְדַּעְזְעוּ אֵיבָרָיו, זֶה בְּחִינַת חֳלִי הַקַּדַּחַת' — the trembling/shaking is an expression of the same fire-and-water dysfunction, the body's physical manifestation of the fever. It belongs to the same package as חולי הקדחת.
additions.source_quote: נִזְדַּעְזְעוּ אֵיבָרָיו, זֶה בְּחִינַת חֳלִי הַקַּדַּחַת, שֶׁבָּא עַל־יְדֵי אֲכִילַת עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה, עַל־יְדֵי מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה כַּנַּ

eitza_concepts_not_included: אכילה יתרה (overeating) — causes fever via eitza, not a bechina of it

מאכל בהמה (animal food) — the Rebbe says overeating IS a bechina of animal food, but this is an eitza to the fever; if added it would be a separate bechina edge between אכילה יתרה and מאכל בהמה, not in this Torah's current dataset
זיעה (sweat) — the cure for the illness, connected by eitza (sweat produces healing), not bechina
שלמות הדעת (wholeness of da'at) — the healed state, eitza result of sweating, not a bechina node in this Torah
analysis_notes.mirror_analysis: Torah #263 has only one package because the Torah is extremely brief (5 lines). The single package is entirely in the evil/negative domain — fever as blemished da'at. The good mirror (שלמות הדעת — wholeness of da'at, restored through sweat/זיעה) is present in the Torah but connected only by eitza relationships, not bechina. There are no bechina edges establishing a positive package.
